The formula records how residue collisions and nilpotent tangent directions jointly determine all local-factor multiplicities, which is strictly more informative than a single full-generation probability or a minimum-generator bound. The square-zero case is the first nonreduced thickening of the product-of-fields setting and admits an exact, self-contained type law.
